summary: Lycophron (Ancient Greek: Λυκόφρων, "wolf-minded") is, in Homeric myth, a Cytherean exile who serves as squire to Telamonian Ajax at Troy. Hector's spear, aimed at Ajax, kills him above the ear beside the ships.
etymology: Ancient Greek Λυκόφρων from λύκος "wolf" and φρήν "mind."

sections.heading: Squire of Ajax
paragraphs: Homer (Iliad 15.429–437) makes Lycophron son of Mastor, a native of Cythera who fled after slaying a man and took refuge with Ajax on Salamis. During the defense of the ships Hector hurls a bright spear at Ajax; it misses the prince and strikes Lycophron on the head, and he falls from the stern into the dust.
He is a battlefield companion defined by exile and patronage, not the Hellenistic poet Lycophron of Chalcis.

sections.heading: Homonym care
paragraphs: The atlas id lycophron-cythera is Ajax's Cytherean squire alone — never the Alexandra poet, nor other minor Lycophrons.
